findings.reason: a coordinator dispatching the implementable sections one beat would dispatch §4 against its 64 GB clause before the only work that lowers that memory has landed, so §4 fails its own gate on the plan's declared order.
findings.text: §8/§9 exist to reduce the read's compile memory, and §4's clause (1) (plan.html:73) requires the read's first call at 132, 300 and 550 cells at most 64 GB of host memory, which the S28 record (data-section s4, job 1337904) says the read exceeds today, yet plan-section-depends-on declares s4:[s2,s3] with no edge to s8/s9 (s9 depends only on s8)

findings.reason: with no declared durable path the two nodes' compile-memory measurements and lowering-test receipts have no home a later reader can open, and the plan's own convention (as in §3 node (b)-(e) and §4 node (a)) assigns one per node, so the delivered evidence has no declared destination.
findings.text: neither §8 (line 90) nor §9 (line 94) names a record document, receipt directory or figure directory

findings.reason: a worker reading §9 is told to meet a 64 GB compile bound the rest of the plan explicitly retires, and the two instructions cannot both be satisfied without the plan saying which supersedes; either §0 must record that the read's compile-memory work re-imposes the bound, or §9 must not bind the cold compile.
findings.text: §9 clause (2) requires "the 132-cell read compiles on the CPU backend within 64 GB", a bound on a cold compile, while §0 (plan.html:48) records that the cold compile "carries no bound" after the 2026-11-18 ruling and §4 clause (2) (plan.html:73) calls it "the cold compile, which this plan no longer bounds"
